issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument messageOnRide() method (signature: messageOnRide(): String) as shown in the UML and example usages (Main.java calls r.messageOnRide()). The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements messageOnRide with a String parameter in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch makes the solution structurally incompatible with the specification and the template usage and will confuse students about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution follow the specification: change the Rideable interface to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters (String messageOnRide()), and update Pig and Seal (and any other implementors) to implement messageOnRide() without parameters, returning the string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intentionally required, update the UML, problem statement examples (including Main.java usage) and template to call messageOnRide(equipment) consistently.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is declared without parameters in the problem statement (UML) and the template's example usage calls messageOnRide() with no arguments, but the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and Pig/Seal implement that signature). This signature mismatch creates a conceptual mapping barrier: students see and are asked to implement/use a parameterless messageOnRide(), yet the solution and some implementations expect an equipment parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's Rideable and its implementations to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters and update implementations accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust example usages to pass an equipment argument. Prefer aligning to the problem/template usage (parameterless) to avoid breaking the provided examples.
